description: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity for two categories, represented by blue and orange bars. The horizontal axis represents the sparsity rate, labeled with values ranging from 10% to 80% in increments of 10%, with no specific scale type indicated. The vertical axis represents perplexity, labeled as "Perplexity" with a logarithmic scale ranging from 10^1 to 10^3. The chart displays grouped bars, with each group corresponding to a specific sparsity rate and containing two bars representing the two categories. The blue bars are labeled as "Per-Output" in the legend, while the orange bars are not explicitly labeled but are represented by a gray square in the legend. The bars are generally short at lower sparsity rates and increase in height as the sparsity rate increases, with the shortest bars at 10% sparsity rate having a perplexity of around 3 and the tallest bars at 80% sparsity rate having a perplexity of approximately 800 for the orange bar and 400 for the blue bar. The bars are sorted in ascending order by sparsity rate, and there is no visual emphasis on any particular bar.
